[ASSISTANT_SAID] Nuclear reactors produce heat by using nuclear reactions to convert the energy of atomic nuclei into electrical energy through controlled fission of uranium atoms.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Nuclear reactors provide a reliable and long-lasting source of power that can operate for many years without refueling, which is advantageous for submarines.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The primary safety mechanism in nuclear reactors is control rods that absorb neutrons to reduce the rate of nuclear fission.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Other safety features of naval nuclear reactors include backup control rods, shielding to prevent radiation escape, pressure and temperature controls, and extensive emergency response plans.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] There have been no serious nuclear accidents on naval vessels since the first nuclear reactor was commissioned in the US Navy in 1954, but there have been minor incidents.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The safety of naval vessel nuclear reactors is consistently re-evaluated and improved to minimize potential risks.
